# SEO, content, and business

Use this reference for search visibility, blogs, editorial operations, analytics, conversions, monetization, and portfolio governance.

## Business and measurement

Define the business model and primary conversion before optimizing traffic: lead, sale, booking, subscription, donation, application, support deflection, readership, or another named outcome. Map conversion events and their data owners. Use a small measurement plan with event name, trigger, properties, consent basis, destination, and decision it informs.

Do not equate traffic with value. Report acquisition, engagement, conversion, revenue or qualified outcome, retention, and cost where the data exists. Separate attribution conventions from causal claims. Run experiments with a stated hypothesis, guardrail metrics, duration/sample rationale, and stopping rule.

## Technical SEO

- Ensure important pages return appropriate status codes, render meaningful indexable content, and have stable descriptive URLs.
- Use unique, accurate titles and useful snippets; keep one clear page purpose rather than mechanically targeting keyword variants.
- Maintain intentional canonicals, redirects, pagination or faceting behavior, robots controls, and XML sitemaps containing preferred canonical URLs.
- Build crawlable internal links and useful hierarchy. Find orphans, redirect chains, broken links, soft 404s, duplicate pages, and accidental noindex rules.
- Add structured data only when it truthfully represents visible content and matches a currently supported vocabulary and search feature. Validate it, but never promise a rich result.
- For JavaScript sites, verify rendered HTML, discovery, caching, metadata, links, and status behavior rather than assuming client execution works for every crawler.

SEO cannot guarantee ranking or indexing. Use Search Console or the relevant engine’s verified data when authorized, and distinguish impressions, clicks, position, indexed state, crawl observations, and third-party estimates.

## Editorial and blog operations

Maintain audience, topic scope, voice, fact-checking, author/reviewer, sources, disclosures, update cadence, taxonomy, internal linking, imagery rights, calls to action, and archive policy. Each article should satisfy a real reader intent and contribute distinct value.

Create a lifecycle: brief → draft → review → accessibility/SEO QA → preview → approval → publish → distribute → measure → refresh/consolidate/retire. Preserve redirects when URLs change. Mark sponsored, affiliate, AI-assisted, or regulated content as required by policy and law.

## Portfolio coordination

Avoid competing sites publishing indistinguishable pages for the same intent unless the brands and audiences genuinely differ. Share design systems, infrastructure, monitoring, and editorial controls where that reduces cost without collapsing necessary brand or data boundaries.

Maintain a quarterly view of each site’s purpose, audience, conversion, traffic quality, content health, technical health, risk, cost, revenue/value, owner, and next decision. Recommend consolidation or retirement from evidence, including redirect, data-export, legal-retention, and domain-renewal plans.
